beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The difference is small enough to measure, yet large enough to shape a life.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Sava's concern remains real, because delayed fear can also expose him to harm.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book gives both sides reasons before asking the reader to choose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ivarra prepares a festival that teaches children how their ancestors survived.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Artificial predator shapes cross the square along carefully arranged routes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The ritual rehearses retreat together, turning remembered danger into public reassurance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Taren pays attention to the cables and details outside that reassuring story.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Something about the arrangement does not fit what he expects.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The opening mystery grows from observation rather than an unexplained prophecy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Read the scene to discover what happens when rehearsal meets an unfamiliar danger.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Long Quiet has lasted four centuries, but it requires continuous maintenance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Weapons, food, births and infrastructure fall within an interdependent political arrangement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Great Hearing correlates data and makes recommendations across that system.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Officials can treat those recommendations as necessities rather than decisions someone must defend.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel asks what disappears when authority speaks in the language of measurement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its answer develops through people who still believe they are preserving life.
